claim: Learning-rate transfer in these hybrids requires not only width-independent update-to-weight ratios, which muP provides, but also that the relative size of updates across components (for example SSM state parameters versus feed-forward weights) stays the same as width grows, and AdamW's per-parameter normalisation provides this automatically while SGD does not, so SSM-specific learning-rate corrections over-correct under AdamW. Supported only if, from width 128 to 256 and 512, the change in the update-size ratio between the SSM A_log parameter and the feed-forward weights is at most about 25% under AdamW with plain muP but above 150% under AdamW with the SSM rules and above 200% under SGD; and if, at fixed parameterisation, the wider model reaches lower loss than the narrower one at every learning rate tested for the adaptive optimisers (AdamW and momentum-free Adam) but at no more than 2 of 7 for SGD with or without momentum.

experiments: Define architectures, schemes and the metric. Setup: layer patterns over Transformer blocks (T: GQA, RoPE, SwiGLU), Mamba blocks (M: selective SSM with conv1d, simplified-ZOH discretisation, state size 16) and parallel hybrid blocks (H); schemes: standard parameterisation (one shared LR), plain muP (embeddings N(0,1), hidden N(0, 1/d), zero head, hidden LR eta/d), block-wise muP adding the SSM rules of Chennuru Vankadara et al. (per-component init and LR in SSM width and state size), and an approximated block-wise variant that keeps the SSM init and eta_C rule but drops eta_A ~ N_u. AdamW (0.9, 0.95), cosine warmup, clipping 1.0; WikiText-2 (2k steps), WikiText-103 (20k), FineWeb-Edu (500M tokens). Transfer gap = relative loss increase at the target when using the proxy's best LR from the grid {0.003, 0.01, 0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3}.

Measure per-component update balance. Setup: MHMH depth 16, state size 16, base LR 1.0, proxy width 128; ratio of per-step update norms for A_log vs FFN and Mamba in_proj vs FFN, averaged over steps 50-200 and 3 seeds; change of that ratio going to widths 256 and 512. Result: A_log / FFN change 20% / 21% for AdamW with plain muP, 166% / 436% for AdamW with the SSM rules, 235% / 342% for SGD with plain muP and 233% / 835% for SGD with the SSM rules; in_proj / FFN 4% / 5%, 15% / 20%, 0% / 0% and 23% / 31%.

Ablate the optimizer and test the SSM rule's premise. Setup: HHHH depth 16 with plain-muP parameter groups, 2k steps on WikiText-103, LRs 0.001-1.0, under AdamW, Adam without momentum, SGD with and without momentum (also weight decay, epsilon, Sophia, Muon variants); step-1 and steady-state width exponents of effective updates for A_log, B, C under SGD. Result: best losses at width 256 / 1,024: AdamW 4.392 / 4.099, momentum-free Adam 4.470 / 4.465, SGD with momentum 7.732 / 7.955, plain SGD 9.398 / 10.803; the wider model is lower at 7/7 LRs for both adaptive optimisers but 1/7 and 2/7 for SGD, so the g / sqrt(v) normalisation, not momentum, is what matters. Under SGD the SSM rules give width-invariant step-1 updates for B (+0.006) and C (+0.029) but amplify A_log (+1.00) because the 1/N_u gradient decay they assume is absent; the invariance of B and C does not survive training (+1.35, +0.71).
